summary: Scenario audit of S01-S10, the 16C shock vectors and overlap checks, and engine v0.1. Q1 (unsupported probabilities): none found; G5 passes. Q2 (double counting): confirmed by in-memory engine probes with synthetic illustrative inputs. The engine adds overlapping real-growth shocks with different timing (S04-d + S05-d in S10). It nulls same-key shocks whose magnitudes conflict, which would silently remove the remittance shock from S10. 16C's fifteen overlap checks are endorsed. New findings: shock units 'pct_change'/'pp' are outside the platform unit registry; the audit adapter mislabels decimal shocks as 'percent'; and unit-channel compatibility is not validated. 01C's challenge is upheld: the engine can apply deflator and FX shocks, but no scenario defines one, so USD-GDP conclusions would omit price and FX channels. Because all magnitudes are null, no current quantitative conclusion is invalidated. Omitted dependencies are listed. Verdict: UNVERIFIED for the scenario set, with a latent calculation inconsistency on units (recorded as dissent).

challenges.text: Please (i) record in S10 an explicit combination rule for components; (ii) add S06 to S10 or state why it is excluded; (iii) propose, for human review, domestic_prices and exchange_rate shocks (01C) and an Indian approval-state variable; (iv) restate shock units using codes registered in units.py or have 00A register 'pct_change'/'pp' there.

Platform-level items for human decision, which 28 does not edit: register the shock unit codes; make scenario_proposal pass the actual shock unit, not 'percent'; add unit-channel compatibility (pp for rate channels) to validate_scenario; stop compose() from dropping the second shock id silently on conflicting magnitudes; state in run_scenario whether same-variable shocks with different keys are additive by design.

Your challenge (no deflator/FX shock) is upheld. Also, PF-4 (valuation-driven) milestones depend on sustained real appreciation. A regional FX shock through the INR peg is the dominant geopolitical risk to that path, so PF-4 results should be labelled valuation-dependent and exposed to an INR/USD stress.
Supplier-continuity is an implicit assumption in S01, S02 and S10. Please propose a supplier-interruption variable separate from price (S01-c) and quantity (S02-c).

uncertainty: Moderate on mechanics (verified by execution). High on dependencies, where the omission list is not exhaustive.

scenario_findings.question: Q1 probabilities
scenario_findings.finding: No scenario YAML assigns a probability. All ten state 'no probabilities are assigned', and no Division B file asserts a numeric probability (27E uses conditional statuses only). G5 passes.

scenario_findings.question: Q2 double counting
scenario_findings.finding: Confirmed by independent engine probes with synthetic illustrative inputs (not estimates): (a) S04-d and S05-d (aggregate_real_growth, different timing keys) are summed additively in S10's first shocked year. run_scenario adds magnitudes per projection variable per year, so the two stack even if both scenarios' GDP effects share a common cause (16C OV-04). (b) S01-a and S04-a share the key (remittances, 1, 2). With equal (null) magnitudes they are 'counted once'. With different magnitudes compose() nulls the merged shock and keeps only S01-a's id, so S10 would silently carry no remittance shock (OV-01). (c) If S04-d/S05-d are kept once BoP or sector modules transmit their own channels, the channel effects and the aggregate override will double count.

scenario_findings.question: Q2 double counting
scenario_findings.finding: 16C's OV-02 (migrant stock/permits vs remittances), OV-03 (seats vs arrivals), OV-05 (price x quantity), OV-06 (total imports vs petroleum), OV-07 (electricity export volume), OV-08 (AI demand vs substitution) and OV-11 (compliance vs formality) are reviewed and endorsed. The proposed rules (min operators, disjoint components, a single joint path) are appropriate. None is implemented in engine v0.1.

scenario_findings.question: shock units
scenario_findings.finding: Scenario and 16C shock units 'pct_change' and 'pp' are not unit codes in src/economic_model/units.py (parse_unit raises), contrary to CLAUDE.md rule 7; 24A raised the same point. src/auditing/proposals.scenario_proposal labels every shock claim unit 'percent', while engine SHOCK_UNITS define both as decimal. Once magnitudes are filled, audit records will mislabel decimal shocks as percent, a 100x scale ambiguity. validate_scenario does not check unit-channel compatibility: a 'pct_change' shock on aggregate_real_growth is accepted and applied as additive percentage points (probe P4).

scenario_findings.question: engine limitation
scenario_findings.finding: The engine can apply three projection channels (aggregate_real_growth, domestic_prices, exchange_rate). No scenario shocks domestic_prices or exchange_rate: S01 and S02 declare exchange_rate without a shock, domestic_prices is declared nowhere, and EXP-10 (exchange rate) has no shock. In practice only S04-d and S05-d can move projections, and 26 of 28 shocks are NOT_MODELLED_IN_PROJECTION. 01C's challenge is upheld: a peg step, an INR/USD shock or oil-price pass-through to the deflator cannot be stress-tested. Because nominal USD GDP inherits INR/USD movements one-for-one under the peg (17A), any scenario conclusion about distance to the US$3T target from S01, S02, S04 or S10 would omit the price and FX channels.
scenario_findings.severity: invalidates USD-GDP conclusions; real-growth conclusions would rest on exogenous overrides

scenario_findings.question: does the limitation invalidate current conclusions
scenario_findings.finding: Not yet. With every magnitude null, every scenario is QUALITATIVE_ONLY and no quantitative conclusion exists to invalidate. Once magnitudes arrive, only real-growth results are interpretable, and only as aggregate overrides. USD-GDP, fiscal, BoP and household conclusions would be invalid until the corresponding modules and deflator/FX shocks exist.

scenario_findings.question: omitted dependencies
scenario_findings.finding: (a) S10 omits S06, although origin- and destination-side migration restrictions co-occurred in the reported 2026 events (E01 with E04). (b) The global_interest_rates channel is unused in all scenarios despite 20A/20C leads. (c) There is no variable for Indian import-side policy (E05), which 17A proposed. (d) Northern-route transit (X10) has no shock (OV-14). (e) S10 assumes continuity of the single petroleum supplier during a regional disruption (22A); S01-c/S02-c do not model supplier-level interruption. (f) S09 depends on the Indian approval state A_t (22E, 27E), but no approval-state shock exists and S02-d stands in for it. (g) Aviation capacity for evacuation and return migration is missing from S01 (19D). (h) US aid volatility is missing from S08/S10 (18A). (i) The telecom/internet backbone single gateway is missing from S03/S07 (16B). (j) The domestic-use case in S09 is not independent of India in the dry season (22E).

scenario_findings.question: unrealistic or inconsistent assumptions
scenario_findings.finding: (a) S10 lists four components but states no rule for how they interact (additive, min or joint path); the engine therefore defaults to key-based merging and per-year additive summation. (b) S01's trigger is HYPOTHETICAL while a similar real 2026 event is reported. If the base year is FY2025/26 or later, applying S01 on top of a baseline that already contains the event double counts (OV-13). (c) Timing keys are offsets from a PENDING base year whose period type (Nepal FY) is not yet fixed, while international evidence is calendar-year (CLAUDE rule 6).
